Company description: The ENTENTE pour la forêt méditerranéenne, known as ENTENTE VALABRE, is an independent public administrative body that works closely with the Ministries of the Interior, Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion (MTECT) and Agriculture. As a key interdepartmental player at both institutional and territorial level, VALABRE's main challenge is to protect people and areas from major natural hazards.
Bringing together 31 local authorities, including 15 départements, 15 Services Départementaux d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) and the Collectivité Territoriale de Corse, its missions focus on the pooling of skills and resources, as well as consultation with its partners, with the aim of optimising the management of major risks. The organisation is divided into 4 departments:
- The Information and Prevention of Major Risks Department ;
- The Civil Security Training School (ECASC);
- The Test and Research Centre (CEREN);
- The Innovation and New Technologies Centre (PONT).
 
The PONT offers its members a suite of technological solutions covering all the needs associated with managing forest fires and fires in natural areas, from prevention to operational response, feedback and continuous improvement. VALABRE is strategically positioned as a provider of shared operational solutions, with a coherent vision at territorial level. The COP CRIMSON, used by the Centre Opérationnel de Gestion Interministérielle des Crises (COGIC), the 7 Centres Opérationnels de Zone de défense (COZ) and more than 50 fired departments, continues to be deployed in France (SDIS, departmental councils, local authorities) and internationally. The CRIMSON tool also provides real-time information to the ORSEC and SYNAPSE national crisis management platforms, making VALABRE the only French entity authorised to supply these Ministry of the Interior networks. Once operational, the NEXIS project, which aims to pool the Alert Management Systems (SGA) and Operational Management Systems (SGO) used in the SDIS, will also incorporate a CRIMSON gateway.
The PONT also keeps a proactive watch on innovative technologies, with the aim of enhancing its services to end users (emergency services, civil protection, inter-municipalities, regional authorities, etc.). For example, PONT was commissioned by MTECT to carry out the PANOPTÈS study, the aim of which is to deploy a system for the early detection (<5 minutes) of all forest fires and fires in natural areas on a national (metropolitan) scale, and to monitor them in near-real time (burnt areas, fire fronts, fire breaks, hot spots, etc.). This early detection is in line with the national operational doctrine of "massive attack on incipient fires".

Swiss TXT AG is a wholly-owned subsidiary of SRG SSR, the Swiss public broadcaster. It serves as the leading competence center for Digital Media Operations and Accessibility for all national Swiss Radio & TV stations.
With a strong emphasis on operations and Cloud Solutions, Swiss TXT AG has been at the forefront of guiding Switzerland into an increasingly complex digital future. For over 35 years, Swiss TXT AG has provided infrastructure, content management, and commercialization services to SRG, including access services such as captions and subtitling for various language areas throughout Switzerland. Notable customers of Swiss TXT AG include SRF 1, SRF zwei, SRF info, RTS Un, RTS Deux, and more.
In the past decade, Swiss TXT AG has expanded its services beyond broadcasters and now caters to companies like SBB and governmental organizations such as Parliaments. Its technical services encompass a wide range of offerings, including 4K delivery via IP, multimedia playout, multi-CDN operations, HbbTV distribution, operation of the Swiss Media Hub, as well as the development and operation of the Swiss national content Exchange for private media houses and publishers. Additionally, in the field of Managed Cloud, Swiss TXT AG provides Storage solutions (6PB), VOD, and the Kaltura Hub Europe.
All distribution channels offered by Swiss TXT AG support live streaming and Video on Demand functionality. The comprehensive backend operation covers the entire workflow, which includes Digital Rights Management (DRM), Encoding Transcoding, Media & Digital Asset Management (MAM/DAM), Transfer & CDN (Content Delivery Network) with multi-CDN functionality.
A dedicated department within Swiss TXT AG focuses on providing access services for foreign languages and people with hearing or visual impairments, utilizing advanced technologies. These access services encompass captioning, subtitling, audio description, and signing. In addition to serving SRG, Swiss TXT AG also extends these services to external customers such as Sky and Pro7. This year, Swiss TXT AG introduced remote access services for individuals with hearing impairments and the deaf community in educational institutions across Switzerland.
Committed to innovation, Swiss TXT AG strives to develop, implement, and operate cutting-edge technologies while maintaining a strong focus on quality. Notably, the company has created the NerStar tool, which measures the quality of live subtitling and is currently utilized by broadcast regulators in various countries including the UK, Canada, Switzerland, and Spain.

entityName: UNB - Radio and Space Physics Laboratory
entityDescription:
The Radio and Space Physics Lab (RSPL) at the University of New Brunswick is involved in several aspects of the near-Earth and planetary space environments, including fundamental and applied ionospheric and space plasma research, ionospheric modeling, and development of radio instruments for ionospheric monitoring. RSPL operates Space Weather Ionospheric Network Canada (SWINCan), one of the world's largest ionospheric observation networks. RSPL includes several research scientists, graduate and undergraduate students, and technical staff. Some specific projects of RSPL are outlined below.
The Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Network (CHAIN) was the original project of RSPL. Since 2008, CHAIN has collected GNSS and high frequency (HF) ionosonde data in order to measure and model the state of the ionosphere spanning polar, auroral, and sub-auroral regions. Currently, there is GNSS data being actively collected from 25 sites across the far north of Canada. CADI data is being collected from 8 sites, co-located with several of the GNSS sites.

SWINCan is the new, expanded ionospheric monitoring network of RSPL, and includes current CHAIN locations. SWINCan is a pan-Canadian network of GNSS receivers and HF sounder systems. This network will be the single largest unified network of GNSS sites in Canada, with 143 locations across the country. HF sounders will be deployed at 20 SWINCan locations. This network will observe the multi-scale structuring and dynamics of the high-latitude ionosphere with unprecedented detail, providing essential measurements to resolve the internal and geospace coupling processes that drive this complex behaviour. SWINCan will also provide essential input for enhancing three-dimensional empirical modeling capabilities of ionospheric plasma density, and for mitigating the effects of space weather on modern technological systems such as position, navigation, and timing (PNT), radio communication, and over-the-horizon-radar, services critical to social, military, science, and major economic sectors.
The Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Models (CHAIM) project involves advanced modelling of the ionosphere. CHAIM incorporates data from CHAIN and several other ground and satellite sources. The Empirical Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Model is the current state-of-the-art for the high latitude ionospheric densities, while assimilative-CHAIM (A-CHAIM) provides the near-real-time ionospheric state by ingesting real-time, multi-source data. CHAIM web applications and software are readily available on the RSPL website.
RSPL is developing next-generation Modular Ionospheric Sounders (MODIS) which will replace the Canadian Advanced Digital Ionosondes (CADIs) being used as part of CHAIN. MODIS systems take advantage of the latest developments in software defined radio and signal processing technology. While providing ionograms and 3D ionospheric drift velocity at a fraction of the cost of current CHAIN ionosondes, MODIS also features scalable coherent timing with nanosecond subsample precision and multi-channel, remote controlled operation. The ionosonde application includes stand-alone and oblique sounding, and permits interdependent experiments with other ground and spaceborne radio systems. The system hardware is designed for operation and maintenance in harsh, remote environments such as the Canadian Arctic.

Little Place Labs strive to become the leader in the relatively new satellite edge computing sector. We create sustainable and scalable advanced software and edge computing capabilities for satellites, with the ultimate mission of exploring, protecting our environment, and improving humanity with our Space-based solutions.
Our core products are special machine learning models that can be deployed and run on remote sensing satellites. Raw imagery and other data would be processed to generate usable insights while in orbit, instead of needing to first download massive amounts of raw data to the ground. This not only saves resources and money but enables near real-time insights for quick responses.
Our technology will help to accelerate and improve the identification and analysis of time-sensitive events (such as forest fires, floods, oil spills, logistics, defense, etc) and optimize the efficiency of the delivery of intelligence to decision-makers on the ground. description: boltzplatz is an engineering service provider and a spin-off from the University of Stuttgart (Germany), offering numerical simulations of rarefied gas and plasma dynamics. At the heart of the company lies the open-source software PICLas, which was originally developed to simulate space systems, including atmospheric entry and in-space propulsion. Thanks to a successful technology transfer, companies in the semiconductor manufacturing and vacuum coating industries developing vacuum and plasma technologies can leverage our numerical simulations. This reduces the need for costly prototypes and extensive testing, saving both time and expenses. Potential applications include the prediction of the performance of vacuum pumps, determination of the gas and plasma distribution in vacuum coating equipment, and the characterization of electron and ion beam properties. Beyond complete simulation projects, boltzplatz offers technical support and software development for PICLas.
entityDescription: boltzplatz is a spin-off from the University of Stuttgart and uses the latest scientific findings in simulation technology to solve problems in high-tech industries such as semiconductor manufacturing and vacuum coating. Their open-source software PICLas allows the treatment of rarefied gas and plasma flows under the influence of electromagnetic fields.
